# SetEntityStencil

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Entities](Blitz3D-Entities)

</div>


```blitzbasic
SetEntityStencil:Void entity:Int32, compare:Int32, reference:Int32=0, read_mask:Int32=255, write_mask:Int32=255, fail:Int32=0, depth_fail:Int32=0, pass:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | In | Int32 | required | Entity handle. |
| `compare` | In | Int32 | required | The comparison, from 0 to 7. |
| `reference` | In | Int32 | `0` | The value compared with and written by replace, from 0 to 255. Default 0. |
| `read_mask` | In | Int32 | `255` | The bits that are compared, from 0 to 255. Default 255. |
| `write_mask` | In | Int32 | `255` | The bits that are written, from 0 to 255. Default 255. |
| `fail` | In | Int32 | `0` | The operation when the comparison fails, from 0 to 7. Default 0 (keep). |
| `depth_fail` | In | Int32 | `0` | The operation when the comparison holds and the depth test fails, from 0 to 7. Default 0 (keep). |
| `pass` | In | Int32 | `0` | The operation when both hold, from 0 to 7. Default 0 (keep). |

## Description

Sets the stencil test of an entity and what it does to the stencil, for cameras with a stencil ([SetCameraStencil](SetCameraStencil)). For every pixel of the entity, `reference And read_mask` is compared with `stencil And read_mask`; the pixel is only drawn if the comparison holds. Then the stencil gets one of three operations, in the bits of `write_mask`: `fail` if the comparison did not hold, `depth_fail` if it held but the depth test did not, and `pass` if both held. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

Comparisons: 0 never, 1 less, 2 equal, 3 less or equal, 4 greater, 5 not equal, 6 greater or equal, 7 always. "Less" means that the reference is less than the stencil.

Operations: 0 keep, 1 zero, 2 replace (with the reference), 3 increment (stops at 255), 4 decrement (stops at 0), 5 invert, 6 increment and wrap, 7 decrement and wrap.

This sets both sides of the triangles; [SetEntityStencilBack](SetEntityStencilBack) gives the back faces their own. Compare 7 with every operation 0, the default, is no stencil at all. Cameras without a stencil ignore all of this.

What the stencil does depends on the order in which things are drawn: the entity that marks the stencil has to be drawn before the ones that test it. Entities with a stencil keep the order they are drawn in, and [EntityOrder](EntityOrder) puts the marking ones first. Entities that use order-independent transparency (`BLITZLLVM_OIT` 1 to 5) ignore the stencil.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 640, 480, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
SetCameraStencil camera, True

; A portal frame that writes 1 to the stencil where it is drawn.
portal = CreateCube()
EntityOrder portal, 1
PositionEntity portal, 0, 0, 10
ScaleEntity portal, 2, 3, 0.1
SetEntityStencil portal, 7, 1, 255, 255, 0, 0, 2

; The world on the other side: only drawn inside the portal.
other = CreateSphere(32)
EntityColor other, 0, 128, 255
PositionEntity other, 0, 0, 20
ScaleEntity other, 6, 6, 6
SetEntityStencil other, 2, 1

; The world on this side: drawn everywhere else.
here = CreateCube()
EntityColor here, 255, 64, 0
PositionEntity here, 0, 0, 20
ScaleEntity here, 6, 6, 6
SetEntityStencil here, 5, 1

While Not KeyHit(1)
	TurnEntity other, 0, 1, 0
	TurnEntity here, 1, 0, 0
	RenderWorld
	Flip
Wend
```
